input_narrative: SYNTHETIC NARRATIVE: Synthetic cardiology ward reported a routine software validation finding for the atrial fibrillation detection pathway. No confirmatory clinician note is on file, but the automated CI validation gate blocked the release candidate before any clinical deployment, so no patient was exposed regardless. No patient-facing exposure occurred and the engineering finding was fully contained pre-release or resolved as a non-event.

evidence_links.relevance_note: Synthetic emergency-response incident record confirming a life-threatening complete atrioventricular block event, release v37. This confirms the severity of the issue and its containment.
EU MDR Annex I, Chapter II, Section 17.4 — Minimum IT security requirements. The incident was contained before clinical deployment and caused no patient exposure.
21 CFR § 820.45 — Device labeling and packaging controls. The incident was contained before clinical deployment and caused no patient exposure.
EU MDR Article 83(1)-(2) — Post-market surveillance system of the manufacturer. The incident was contained before clinical deployment and caused no patient exposure.
EU MDR Annex I, Chapter II, Section 17.2 — Software development lifecycle and cybersecurity. The incident was contained before clinical deployment and caused no patient exposure.

risk_report.rationale: The synthetic cardiology ward incident was contained before clinical deployment and caused no patient exposure. The engineering finding was fully resolved as a non-event, with the release candidate blocked by the CI/CD quality gate.
